github.title: Add shallow bundle support for large cases
github.author: jerridan

identity.head: ad382f4919a41dc159a095a55fcd01e39882b5ab
identity.description:
Add shallow bundle support for large cases

## What

- `cloneCase` reads an optional `shallow` file in a case. When it is present, the eval fetches `repo.bundle` into an empty repo that holds the same shallow marks, because git refuses to clone a bundle made from a shallow repo.
- `scripts/make-case.sh` writes `shallow` into the case when the source repo is shallow, and gives the bundle step the shallow marks so it does not stop at a missing object.
- New `scripts/fetch-pr.sh <url> <merge-base> <head> <dir>`: a shallow repo that holds the merge base, the head and the commits between them, and nothing older.
- README: the `shallow` file and the fetch script. Version 0.3.1.

## Why

D5 builds the first case set from Martian and ReviewBench. A full clone of sentry or cal.com makes a bundle of hundreds of megabytes. Two snapshots of the tree are 30 to 60 MB.

## Tests

Two new tests in `test/eval-case.test.ts`: a shallow case checks out; the same bundle without the shallow file is rejected with the case name. Two in `test/eval-scripts.test.ts`: `fetch-pr.sh` then `make-case.sh` gives a case that `cloneCase` checks out with the three-dot diff available; `fetch-pr.sh` stops when the directory exists. `npm test` 1169 passed, lint, typecheck and build exit 0.

triage.summary: The change lets the eval handle cases made from shallow repos. A new script, fetch-pr.sh, makes a shallow repo that holds a PR's merge base and head. make-case.sh now writes a shallow file into the case, and cloneCase uses it to init an empty repo, copy the shallow marks and fetch the bundle. It also adds tests, README docs and a version bump to 0.3.1.

findings.claim: In the shallow branch, `git init` succeeds on a target that already exists and is not empty, where `git clone` fails on it. So a stale or existing repo at `into` gets reused without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the init, check that the target does not exist or is empty, and fail the same way as clone does.
findings.explanation: The shallow and non-shallow paths treat an existing target differently. In the shallow path, refs and the shallow file are written over an existing repo with no error.

findings.claim: The README says a case has four files, but the table now lists an optional fifth file, `shallow`.
findings.evidence: A case is one directory with four files:
findings.suggested_fix: Write "A case is one directory with four files and an optional `shallow` file:".
findings.explanation: The change adds `shallow` to the table, so the stated count of files is now wrong.

findings.claim: The url, base and head arguments reach git without a `--` separator or a sha check, so a value that starts with `-` is read as a git option.
findings.suggested_fix: Check that base and head are hex shas, with a test such as [[ $base =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]. Put `--` before url in `remote add`.
findings.explanation: An argument that is not checked can add git options, for example --upload-pack.

findings.claim: The base and head arguments go to git fetch with no `--` and no sha check, so a value that starts with '-' is read as an option.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the fetch, check that base and head match ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$.
findings.explanation: A crafted argument such as --upload-pack=... can make git run a command, and the script does not validate its arguments.

findings.claim: No test checks that the final depth cut leaves no commit older than the merge base.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert that the shallow file lists the merge base, or that `git rev-list --count head2` equals count + 1.
findings.explanation: The test checks only the count of base..head, so it still passes if the cut is removed and older history stays in the bundle.

findings.claim: No test covers the error path where base is not an ancestor of head within 1000 commits.
findings.evidence: echo "fetch-pr: $base is not an ancestor of $head within 1000 commits" >&2
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that passes a base that is not an ancestor and asserts a non-zero exit and the message.
findings.explanation: This new error branch has no test, so a broken exit or loop would go unnoticed.

first.rationale: The behavioral difference is real: `git init` reinitializes an existing directory where `git clone` fails on a non-empty one. All three callers pass fresh temp-dir paths (`join(root, c.name)`, `join(tmp, "repo")`), so it cannot cause a bug today.

escalated.rationale: The claim is technically true: `git init` succeeds on a directory that already exists, and `git clone` does not. But every caller passes a fresh path inside a new mkdtemp directory, so the target is never stale and there is no bug in practice. The finding has little value.

final.rationale: The claim is technically true: `git init` succeeds on a directory that already exists, and `git clone` does not. But every caller passes a fresh path inside a new mkdtemp directory, so the target is never stale and there is no bug in practice. The finding has little value.
